messages:
jamie: Quick heads-up — ran an initial onboard smoke for tidepool-v2-embed (FP16 -> int6). Baseline (opal-v1) recall@10 on docs_longtail was 0.842; tidepool int6 came back 0.775. That's larger than I expected on the long-tail set. Anyone seen similar?

sasha: Can you paste the exact eval command + config? :eyes:

jamie: Sure — this is what I used:
```bash
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model tidepool-v2 \
  --quant int6 \
  --norm none \
  --dataset docs_longtail \
  --k 10 \
  --batch 512 \
  --seed 42
```

eval-bot: job 4998 finished — summary:
 recall@1: 0.612
 recall@5: 0.701
 recall@10: 0.775
 mean_pos_cos: 0.421
 mean_neg_cos: 0.187
 silhouette_k10: 0.18

liam: Hmm, that recall delta (~0.07) is concerning. Do you have cluster-level stats or sim distributions? Could be centroid shift from quantization.

jamie: I grabbed a few quick stats — distribution shifted lower for positives: mean_pos_cos (FP16 baseline) was 0.493 vs 0.421 here. Cluster coverage (kmeans 200) dropped: pct clusters with >=5 members 0.73 -> 0.58.

maria: Did you apply L2 normalization after quantization? We saw earlier that int6 artifacts were hurting raw cosines but normalization often recovers most of it.

jamie: Good catch — I ran without norm (see --norm none). Re-ran with post-quant L2 normalize and the numbers improved:
```bash
python tools/eval_embeddings.py --model tidepool-v2 --quant int6 --norm l2 --dataset docs_longtail --k 10 --batch 512 --seed 42
```

eval-bot: job 5000 finished — summary:
 recall@1: 0.638
 recall@5: 0.761
 recall@10: 0.831
 mean_pos_cos: 0.472
 mean_neg_cos: 0.192
 silhouette_k10: 0.23

sasha: That's much better — suggests the quantized representation needs explicit postprocess normalization. We should add that as a required step in the onboarding checklist for all intX quant runs. :+1:

liam: Agreed. Also worth running centroid-shift check between FP16 and int6 — compute mean cosine between corresponding centroids and flag if shift > 0.02. If clusters move, that explains recall drop for long-tail queries.

jamie: On it. I'll run centroid drift + seed stability (3 seeds) and stratify recall by query length and frequency. Quick sample of idflip cases I saw (query -> top hit FP16 / int6):
```
Q: "how to migrate db schema"
FP16 top: doc_3245 (score 0.72)
int6 top: doc_1289 (score 0.62)  <-- semantically further

Q: "oauth token refresh error"
FP16 top: doc_998 (score 0.69)
int6 top: doc_998 (score 0.67)  <-- stable
```

maria: If the idflips concentrate on low-frequency docs, we might tolerate small regressions but should quantify business impact. Also add silhouette and purity thresholds to the PR template.

jamie: Scheduling the extra runs on 2x A10s now; ETA ~45m. Will paste full diffs + plots when done. Tagging @maria for checklist update.

eval-bot: job 5001 started (centroid-drift, 3 seeds)

jamie: Thanks — will follow up with recall-by-length and a short summary for the release notes (include recommended default: post-quant L2 normalize + centroid check).
